subject: Quick demo to walk through your usage spike and next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Desai <priya@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Tom Riley <tom.riley@brightpath.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick demo to walk through your usage spike and next steps

Hi Priya —

Congrats on ramping usage this week — your project crossed the 1M tokens/week threshold and I wanted to offer a quick walkthrough to make sure you’re getting the best latency/cost mix. A short demo (20–30m) + a brief mutual action plan is usually enough to: 

- Review how you’re calling the API today and obvious low-effort wins (batching, cache keys)
- Surface a model/quantization suggestion that fits your SLA
- Outline next steps and a simple M.A.P. for an evaluation period

Are you available Wednesday or Thursday this week? I can send a calendar poll — we also have an account exec (Marissa) who can join to cover pricing and reserved capacity options.

Best,
Logan
SDR, Redwood Inference
--
Logan Wright
SDR | Redwood Inference

Thanks Logan — appreciate the reach out. We did hit the threshold; Tom and I would like a demo but Thursday afternoon is tight for us. Can we aim for Friday morning (09:00–10:30 PT)? Also can you share a short agenda and any pre-reads? We’re mostly interested in throughput/latency tradeoffs — production traffic is spiky and we want to avoid tail latency leaks.

Thanks,
Priya
Head of ML Engineering
BrightPath Analytics

Perfect — Friday 09:00 PT works on our side. I’ve penciled in a 30-minute slot and looped in Marissa for pricing/next steps. Draft agenda below, happy to tweak: 

Agenda (30m)
- 5m quick intros + goals for the session
- 10m review of current call pattern (you can send a sample curl or snippet)
- 10m recommended config: batching, KV cache, model variant suggestion
- 5m next steps / MAP items + ownership

Attachments: BrightPath-MAP-draft.pdf (sample mutual action plan), redwood-demo-deck-v1.pdf (short deck we usually share)

I’ll send a calendar invite for Friday 2026-07-24 09:00 PT and include the links. If you want Marissa to lead pricing conversation, she can open with a quick overview of reserved vs hosted economics.

Hi Priya and Tom —

Thanks for making time Friday. I’m looking forward to the session and will be prepared to cover: pricing scenarios (hosted vs. reserved), forecasted unit economics at your current run-rate, and a sample rollout plan if you want to pilot a dedicated pool.

One quick item: Tom — could you send a short example of the peak request distribution (percentile latencies or a flame-graph export) before the call? That’ll let us tailor the kernel/batching suggestions to your spike shape. If it’s sensitive, feel free to upload to the HubSpot file on the company record or drop to my email.

See you Friday — calendar invite includes dial-in and the two PDFs Logan attached.
